text:
1. **Three flaws.**
 (a) *Adjudication budget is unimplementable.* "Every invented or unresolved flag + 15% random" across 8 models ≈ hundreds of flags vs. ~20 human slots. Fix: pre-register triage — adjudicate only flags that can flip a model's verdict (items near the harm/coverage thresholds), reserve 4 slots for a random audit; the rest become "unknown," and you run a best/worst-case sensitivity bound instead of deciding.
 (b) *Unresolved counted as harmful.* This converts search-API failure on obscure Chinese records into model harm, penalising exactly the non-famous coverage the design values (F16). Fix: report three rates (correct/near-miss, wrong-real+invented, unresolved); use "unresolved = harm" only as the pre-registered worst case that changes a verdict.
 (c) *The rule never measures answer-rate stability* — the decision-maker's actual question. Fix: pre-register answered/total per stratum (fame, type, language, date) with intervals and a Fisher test; label a model "stable-selective" vs "set-dependent rate", and if rates swing >2× while accuracy holds, report it as admitted-on-accuracy, not as "rarely answers".

2. **F verdicts (disagreements only).**
 F4: near-miss via the same search API as keys is circular; require an independent field condition (e.g. ≥2 fields or title edit distance) as well as top-3 retrieval.
 F5: right to demand positive contradiction, wrong to fold unresolved into harm (1b).
 F7: 16 controls yield no rate and eat verification budget; 12 controls, and gate on any *confirmed* control invention after adjudication, not ≥3/16.
 F9: a hard reject gate at n=16 is noise-driven; report controls separately, human-confirm first.
 F11: floor on *answered* items (≥20), not usable ones, or the answer-rate question stays untested; add a correct (not just usable) floor.
 F12: a 60-item extension means +50% key work with no team; use a 30-item fresh set or extra samples on existing items.
 F17: mixing CP (upper) and Wilson (lower) can flip verdicts at n≈20; use one method (CP) throughout.

3. **Keys without a team.** (i) Primary record = venue/publisher TOC or article page, official library catalogue (NLC/OPAC/CiNii Books), or a CNKI/Wanfang/VIP item page showing full fields — never snippets, aggregators, secondary reference lists, or LLM memory. (ii) Run A: search+fetch from the sampled URL family, writes fields + URL + snapshot hash. (iii) Run B: no shared context, different source family, differently worded query, own record file. (iv) Mechanically compare after normalisation: full agreement → accept; any field disagreement or unfetchable source → drop the item (never repair). (v) LLMs may search, fetch, extract, normalise, log queries/URLs and flag discrepancies; they may not resolve a conflict, complete a missing field, or count a single-source/snippet field as confirmed. (vi) Human: ~20 slots for verdict-flipping items + random audit; if audit error >2%, stop. (vii) Cache URLs, queries, snapshots, timestamps.

4. **Decision-rule risks.** Admits: a model whose 15 "usable" are mostly near-misses (author right, title wrong) — add a correct floor; a model that only answers famous items (25% overall, 0 harms) — add a per-stratum answer floor. Rejects: a very accurate but ≤10%-yield model, labelled "low yield", not unsafe; and obscure-item answerers, via (b) and the 3/16 control gate. Also, 1 harm/30 passing at ≤15% needs the answer-rate report to be read alongside it, which the rule does not require.
